abstraction_design.rationale: The genuinely shared, high-variation pieces (cards across four pages, move tables across methods, sections) are well abstracted; the creep is confined to per-filter wiring in home.tsx, MoveTable internals, and the page-shell markup that an Items page would duplicate.

findings.issue: Filters are uncontrolled inputs reconciled with the URL through two imperative effects (a mount-time pre-hydration catch-up that enumerates each filter by name, plus a DOM-sync effect); a new filter needs ~6 coordinated edits in one file and a missed one fails silently.
findings.suggestion: Drive the controls from a single declarative filter spec (key → param name, parse/serialize) and render controlled inputs, so adding a filter is one entry in one table.

findings.issue: Same ref-plus-two-effects pattern for the Game select (pre-hydration catch-up plus manual value syncing); the select's state is implicitly shared between React and the DOM.
findings.suggestion: Make the select controlled from loaderData and navigate on change only; or extract the home/pokemon URL-syncing into one shared hook so the pattern is documented once.

findings.issue: The 'English short_effect, else latest English flavor text, else —' fallback is duplicated in ability.tsx:20-23; a spec change to the fallback rule lands twice.
findings.suggestion: Add effectOrFlavor(entries: {short_effect, language}[], flavorTexts) to app/app/lib/format.ts and use it from both loaders.

findings.issue: The COLUMNS abstraction (line 24) only drives headers/aria-sort; tbody cells are hardcoded in the same order with a showLevel flag, so adding/removing a column requires three coordinated edits in one file.
findings.suggestion: Render tbody cells from the same column config (cell renderers per column) so headers, sorting and body stay in lockstep.

findings.issue: The catch-all route's component renders null; the actual 'Not found' UI lives in root.tsx:51-66, so editing routes/not-found.tsx visibly changes nothing — a trap for the next maintainer.
findings.suggestion: Render the not-found UI directly in the catch-all route module (keeping the 404 throw for unmatched resource names), and keep root's ErrorBoundary for errors only.

findings.issue: The Move API response shape is declared both here and in move.tsx:8-19; a change to how moves are read from the API means editing each route's local type.
findings.suggestion: Move shared API record types (Move, NamedResource-derived shapes) into app/app/lib/types.ts.

findings.issue: Transport concerns (base URL, cache, fetch) and view-model shaping (speciesCard/pokemonCards/typeInfo) share one module, so data-presentation changes and data-source changes both churn the same file.
findings.suggestion: Split the derived card/type helpers into app/app/lib/cards.ts, leaving api.server.ts as pure transport plus the raw index.

findings.issue: versionGroupOrders() fetches every version-group record per Pokémon page and lives inside a route module, so a second consumer (e.g. an Items page with game data) would copy it.
findings.suggestion: Move it into api.server.ts alongside getIndex so the cache and fetch conventions are shared.

summary: A well-shaped framework-mode app on the current stable React Router: all data access sits behind one server-only module, and the hard cross-cutting pieces (Pokémon cards, move tables, sections, the derived index) are genuinely reusable, so most fixes and the data-source change land in one obvious place. The main editability costs are the two imperative URL/DOM-sync effects that make filter changes subtle and per-filter wiring flag-heavy, plus small duplications (effect fallback, Move type) and a confusing not-found indirection. Every scenario below touches only a small, findable set of files.
